candidate_relations.rationale: The local-file and explicit-target contract clause strengthens the broader installer-runner proposition that rd_install.py consumes exact local inputs rather than selecting or retrieving releases.
The operation-delegability classification explicitly admitting exact non-root disable while excluding protected operations strengthens the operator-management delegation boundary.
The bounded-grant contract's protected-root and other non-delegable exclusions strengthen the operator-management rule that protected-root transfer cannot be delegated.
The Phase 6 parity report's unchanged Phase-1 and Phase-3 candidates strengthen the accepted Phase 6 baseline's parity PASS proposition.
The invalid fixture lacking primary provenance for a non-derived observation strengthens the output-schema proposition that such observations require primary provenance.
Project-v2 compatibility tests that accept valid v2 configuration and reject invalid identity strengthen the Distiller entrypoint's v2 identity-validation proposition.

The greenfield first-invocation workflow remains a valid conformance workflow only against the specification defining exact evidence, byte preservation, immutable submission, and the stop-before-reconciliation boundary.
Production-invocation tests that leave authority and Canon unchanged strengthen the greenfield first-invocation specification's stop-before-reconciliation/admission boundary.
Steward-authorization tests rejecting unauthorized operators and invalid targets strengthen the runtime proposition that operator and role state are validated before authorization changes.
Rupi update tests preserving project-owned authority and stopping on drift strengthen the installer-runner ownership boundary around only the managed root and recovery material.
Failed-update rollback and absence of surfaced authority setup strengthen the installer contract's exclusion of project authority and other project-owned state from installer mutation.
Recovery tests that avoid touching project-owned files on malformed state strengthen the installer ownership boundary.

The CLI contract's explicit adapter-only, no-new-semantic-or-authority-layer boundary strengthens the broader Human-to-Agent proposition that conversation and adapters cannot create extra semantic operations or authority.
Shared-orchestration tests returning an approval boundary instead of manufacturing authority strengthen the Human-to-Agent no-authority principle.
Shared-orchestration tests that refuse non-delegable proposals strengthen the operator-management protected-root delegation boundary.
Rupi end-to-end tests covering protected authority separation, state-preserving updates, durable resume, and no fake mutation strengthen the broad Rupi implementation conformance record.
The original greenfield trial stopping rather than inventing undefined bootstrap scaffolding strengthens the bootstrap fail-closed proposition against unauthorized repair or mutation.
Mutation tests for exact approval binding, append/replay, digest determinism, and idempotent retries strengthen the mutation runtime's proposal/approval validation proposition.
Human-Agent tests that keep explicit adapter boundaries strengthen the CLI contract's adapter-over-shared-primitives architecture.
Focused Rupi update/recovery tests strengthen the end-to-end proposition that verified updates preserve project-owned state.
Failed-update and no-fake-authority tests strengthen the Rupi end-to-end proposition that lifecycle handling does not manufacture readiness or authority.
